summary: The AI Security and Innovation Act amends the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 to establish a Center for AI Security and Innovation within the National Institute of Standards and Technology. The new center is tasked with measuring artificial intelligence risks, facilitating information exchange between non-governmental entities and federal agencies, ensuring U.S. leadership in AI research and evaluation, and supporting the development of technical standards without granting the center any regulatory or enforcement authority.

affected_groups.effect: May enter into voluntary agreements with the Center to evaluate frontier AI systems, share information that remains exempt from public disclosure and government regulation, and participate in consultations regarding standards.
affected_groups.group: Artificial Intelligence Developers and Covered Entities

affected_groups.effect: Responsible for establishing the Center, appointing a director within three months, hiring up to 15 critical technical experts, conducting studies, and submitting annual reports to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Department of Commerce and NIST Personnel

key_provisions: Establishes the Center for AI Security and Innovation within the National Institute of Standards and Technology no later than 60 days after enactment, operating with an authorization of $20,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2032 and sunsetting after five years.

Directs the Center's director to evaluate security measures against specific AI risks, establish voluntary agreements with entities to evaluate frontier AI systems for national and economic security risks, and support NIST laboratories in publishing standards and best practices.
Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to appoint up to 15 critical technical experts for the Center with specialized pay flexibility, bypassing standard government compensation limitations.

Prohibits the Center's director, the Secretary, and the Under Secretary from exercising any regulatory, rulemaking, or enforcement authority, and bars the use of shared information by any level of government to regulate entities.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce to submit an annual report beginning in fiscal year 2027 covering the Center's budget, consultations, goals, international competition assessments, and personnel gaps.
Permits international engagement and talent exchanges with similar foreign centers, explicitly excluding entities located in foreign adversaries.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact criteria that will define a 'covered frontier system'.
Comprehensive baseline data on current artificial intelligence capabilities of U.S. entities compared to foreign adversaries beyond what the director will assess.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The AI Security and Innovation Act amends the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 to establish a Center for AI Security and Innovation within the National Institute of Standards and Technology. The new center is tasked with measuring artificial intelligence risks, facilitating information exchange between non-governmental entities and federal agencies, ensuring U.S. leadership in AI research and evaluation, and supporting the development of technical standards without granting the center any regulatory or enforcement authority.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a specialized federal center focused on AI security, risk measurement, and voluntary standards. It creates mechanisms for public-private cooperation on frontier artificial intelligence systems while explicitly withholding any new regulatory or enforcement powers from the administering agencies.
